## Purpose
The three exemplars in `src/lib/types/` (`economy.ts`, `specs.ts`, `trace.ts`) each declare one or more `Trace(Kind)`/`EconomyScope(Kind)`/`Stage`/`Outcome`-style string-literal unions whose sole job is to mirror a `#[serde(rename_all = "...")]` Rust enum byte-for-byte. These are the vocabulary types every other DTO in the file switches/matches on (`TraceKind` gates `TraceNode.kind`, `EconomyScope["kind"]` derives `EconomyScopeKind`). They exist so the frontend never invents a variant the backend doesn't know, and so a `switch` over them stays exhaustive.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/lib/types/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 3
Each kind type is a plain `export type X = "a" | "b" | ...;` (or, for discriminated unions like `EconomyScope`, a `{ kind: "..."; ...fields }` union with a companion `export type XKind = X["kind"];` derived type) placed near the top of the file, directly above the interfaces that reference it. A one-to-three-line doc comment above the type states which Rust type/module it mirrors and whether the wire casing is snake_case or kebab-case — every one of the three exemplars does this. Values are the literal wire strings, never camelCase.

## How to apply
A new kind type goes in the same `src/lib/types/<domain>.ts` file as the DTOs it discriminates (create a new domain file only when no existing one fits, following the same header-comment style pointing at the mirrored Rust path). Name it `<Domain><Kind>` (e.g. `TraceKind`, `EconomyScopeKind`) or a domain-specific name matching the Rust type name (`Stage`, `Outcome`) when the Rust side has no generic "Kind" suffix — match the Rust identifier, don't invent an English gloss. If the union backs a discriminated object union, derive the bare kind list via `X["kind"]` rather than retyping the literals by hand (see `EconomyScopeKind` in `economy.ts`).
